source_refs.role: FTS5/vector hybrid store and retrieval implementation

mechanism_findings.finding: Project-Frankenstein already implemented a multi-layer persistent memory stack spanning conversational FTS/vector memory, Titan graph retrieval, consciousness retrieval, world-experience context and learned user preferences behind a MemoryHub API.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Strong architectural ancestor for Frank v0.1: preserve logical multi-surface retrieval, but map it into current UnifiedDB/ClayGraph semantics with explicit provenance, user scope and replay receipts rather than treating one fused context string as truth.

mechanism_findings.finding: chat_memory.py implements genuine intra-chat RRF over FTS5 and cosine-vector ranks, while memory_hub.py performs a second-stage cross-layer sort over preassigned per-item RRF-like scores rather than recomputing true cross-source RRF lists.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Reuse hybrid retrieval as a baseline, but instrument actual retrieval provenance and per-source rank contribution before using retrieval fusion as a causal memory mechanism.

mechanism_findings.finding: MemoryHub source attribution for hybrid chat results is heuristic: the first five returned hybrid items are labeled chat_vector and later items chat_fts even though _hybrid_search_history returns already-fused rows without the winning source path.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Current Frank/Clay memory receipts need exact retrieval-path attribution, not inferred labels, so later causal localization can distinguish lexical, vector, graph, user-state and GWT contributions.

mechanism_findings.finding: The memory consolidator implemented bounded recursive abstraction: live turns -> Tier-2 summaries -> Tier-3 essences, with a local Qwen 2.5 3B compression path and extractive fallback.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: Reusable-with-adaptation memory compaction pattern for small-context Frank v0.1, provided raw evidence remains durable and every abstraction retains reversible provenance.

mechanism_findings.finding: Preference extraction is fast and local but stores normalized key/value preferences without an explicit user/person identity dimension in the user_preferences schema; preference provenance is only a coarse source field plus timestamps/confidence.
mechanism_findings.current_mapping: For Andreas-Frank, user-specific memory must be namespaced and provenance-scoped so historical Gabriel/user material cannot bleed into Andreas state. Preference extraction should create candidate facts/preferences with source-message lineage and contradiction/update semantics, not silent global profile truth.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.finding: memory_consolidator._archive_old_messages claims original text remains searchable in the FTS5 index, but chat_memory.py defines an AFTER UPDATE trigger that deletes the old FTS row and inserts the new text. Replacing message text with '[archived]' therefore removes the original lexical content from FTS5.

reproduction.method: isolated in-memory SQLite reproduction using the same external-content FTS5 table plus INSERT and UPDATE trigger logic

negative_results_and_failure_modes.impact: Old compressed messages lose lexical retrieval even though the code comment promises otherwise.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.finding: Tier-3 essence rows record source_msg_ids as Tier-2 abstraction IDs, then delete those Tier-2 rows. The direct message->Tier-2->Tier-3 source chain therefore becomes non-dereferenceable after compaction; turn_start/turn_end retain only a coarse range.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.impact: Abstraction provenance and exact replay/audit are weakened, conflicting with current evidence-preserving ClayGraph/UnifiedDB requirements.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.finding: Embeddings are not removed when text becomes '[archived]'; vector search joins embeddings back to the current messages.text. A semantically matching archived embedding can therefore retrieve the marker text instead of the historical message content.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.impact: Semantic retrieval may spend context budget on an opaque marker and cannot reconstruct the evidence that produced the embedding without a separate immutable raw-content store.

negative_results_and_failure_modes.finding: The historical chat/preference schema is session-aware but not explicitly person/user-identity scoped. In a single-user prototype this can work; in Andreas-Frank migration it is insufficient to guarantee separation from prior creator/test-user state.
negative_results_and_failure_modes.impact: Identity contamination risk unless current Frank state uses hard user namespaces and migration filters.

reuse: Hybrid lexical + semantic retrieval with deterministic measured fusion as a baseline.
Multi-layer memory routing behind one logical query surface.
Bounded recursive abstraction for context reduction.
Local embedding/compression execution and explicit retrieval latency metrics.
Nightly integrity checks and embedding backfill as operational resilience patterns.
must_change: Keep immutable raw message/evidence content separate from compacted context representations.
Preserve transitive provenance from every summary/essence back to immutable source message IDs/hashes.
Do not infer retrieval source labels after fusion; persist exact scorer/source contributions.
Namespace all personal memory/preferences by Frank entity + human user identity + source provenance.
Treat auto-extracted preferences as candidates with evidence/contradiction/update semantics, not unqualified profile truth.
Regression-test lexical and vector retrieval before/after compaction.
recommended_discriminating_tests: H1 memory compaction differential: ingest a frozen conversation corpus, retrieve lexical/vector targets before compaction, run Tier-2/Tier-3 compaction, then require equivalent evidence-bearing retrieval after compaction with intact source IDs/hashes.

H1 identity-isolation test: load synthetic Gabriel and Andreas histories containing contradictory preferences and require zero cross-user retrieval/profile contamination under normal, semantic-neighbor and fallback queries.
Retrieval attribution test: for every injected memory item, log exact contributing retrievers/ranks/scores and replay the context build deterministically.

branch_feedback.frank: DELTA: historical memory stack is a strong reusable ancestor, but Andreas-Frank requires immutable raw evidence, strict user namespaces and replayable provenance across every compaction/retrieval step.
branch_feedback.harness: DELTA: add compaction-retention, archived-vector, source-attribution and Gabriel-vs-Andreas identity-isolation regression tests to H1.
branch_feedback.claycode: DELTA: memory abstractions need explicit source-ref/hash lineage, user/entity scope, immutable/raw vs derived state type separation and reversible compaction semantics.
branch_feedback.claygraph: DELTA: represent derived memory nodes with transitive provenance edges to immutable source events; deleted intermediate summaries must not sever ancestry.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: DELTA: separate immutable event/raw-content plane from derived summaries/embeddings/preferences while retaining one logical query identity and source lineage.
branch_feedback.gwt: DELTA: workspace memory injection should expose causal source attribution so uptake/effect/re-entry can be tied to the actual memory channel used.
branch_feedback.emergenz: NO_CHANGE: this shard establishes memory/provenance mechanisms and defects, not a new causal-emergence result.
branch_feedback.hyperposition: DELTA: multiple retrieval candidates can remain set-valued until context packing; provenance should survive selection rather than collapsing early into one unlabeled string.
branch_feedback.clayresearch: DELTA: preserve memory compaction as a useful historical mechanism but elevate immutable evidence lineage and identity isolation to architectural invariants.
branch_feedback.q12_index: DELTA: recovered historical memory implementation contains both reusable architecture and concrete compaction/retrieval defects; no duplicated reusable-hours credit assigned yet.
